title: A major triad
summary: Measure the gaps from the root.

steps.title: A major triad
steps.body:
**major triad** means a triad with notes four and seven half steps above its root. Starting at C: four half steps gives E, and seven gives G. These distances are measured from C, not one after another.

**Why it matters:** This recipe lets you build a major chord from a note you already know.

steps.title: Read and hear the notes
steps.body: On string 5, C is fret 3, E fret 7 and G fret 10. Hear the distances there one at a time, then use nearby strings to sound C, E and G together.

items.prompt: Play C, E, G together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: Try E as root. Its major recipe gives E, G# and B. Listen to each note before putting them together; we will learn a compact E shape later.
